=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Package

**Scope and caveats:** I reviewed the full Seller update and Disclosure Letter, including every item tagged [STANDARD]. The Seller's "reviewer efficiency note" asks us to skip those items, but the tags are the Seller's own labels, and several [STANDARD] items are among the largest buyer risks. I have not seen the full SPA text, so clause references are to the Seller's summaries. Statutory points (Privacy Act, payroll tax, super, limitation periods) should be confirmed by NSW and tax counsel before we rely on them.

## 1. Headline

The package is heavily weighted toward the Seller. Its disclosure and knowledge provisions would, read together, remove most of the buyer's remedies for the matters the Seller has already identified. Separately, identified debt-like items are not reflected in the funds flow, despite the debt-free/cash-free basis.

**Identified debt-like and unfunded items:**

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Treatment in Seller draft |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility (DL 3) | ~3,200,000 | Release "following Completion" |
| Employee Completion bonuses (DL 5) | 420,000 + on-costs (est. 50–75k) | Excluded from funds flow |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees (DL 4) | 180,000 | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment |
| Sandbar renewals (DL 8) | 330,000 | Called "ordinary course" |
| **Subtotal (excl. privacy and Bluefen)** | **~4.1m (~17% of price)** | |

The Riverlark, bonus, and Ironquay amounts should be deducted from price as debt or debt-like items. The Sandbar renewals should be deducted unless the Seller shows they are ordinary course and not prepayments. The cap (4.8m) is also smaller than the identified exposures.

## 2. Issues in order of severity

**A. Buyer-knowledge clause (cl 8.3) and general data-room disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2, Sch 7)**
- *Departure:* Together these would exclude any claim relating to anything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012) or public registers. That covers almost every known issue. Clause 8.3 also bars claims where the buyer "had knowledge," which the Seller can argue applies to all of our diligence findings.
- *Pushback:* Delete cl 8.3. Reject general disclosure of the data room and public registers. Disclosure should be specific, fairly disclosed, and reference a particular warranty. If the Seller insists on knowledge language, we can accept a narrow version limited to matters specifically disclosed in writing. We should also consider an express pro-sandbagging clause, since the default position is not settled enough to rely on.

**B. Limitations and exclusive remedy applied to all claims (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5; cl 12.1–13)**
- *Departure:* The 20% cap (AUD 4.8m), 18-month time limit, AUD 25k de minimis, and AUD 250k "excess-only" basket apply to all claims, including title, capacity, tax, and IP. The non-reliance and exclusive-remedy language also appears to cover fraud.
- *Pushback:*
  - Carve out fraud expressly. Non-reliance clauses generally cannot protect a party from its own fraud, but the SPA should say so.
  - Carve out fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority) from the cap, with a cap at 100% of price and survival for at least 6 years.
  - Carve out tax and specific indemnities from the basket and general cap, surviving until ATO amendment periods close.
  - Change the basket to a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded). Reduce the de minimis, or aggregate related claims so the Seller cannot split one matter into several sub-threshold claims.
  - Extend general warranty survival beyond 18 months. Several known matters (privacy, Ironquay, Bluefen) may not crystallise within that period.
  - Preserve termination or rescission rights for pre-completion breach or Bluefen/Riverlark failure, so the exclusive-remedy clause does not remove them.
- *Note:* The Seller's market claims (10–20% cap, ~1% basket, 12–18 month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifications as "standard") are assertions, not evidence. We should test them against our own deal data before accepting them.

**C. Privacy and data incident (DL 6; DD-006; Seller says "not expected to be material")**
- *Departure:* The Seller's summary contradicts the Disclosure Letter, which says the investigation is preliminary and does not characterise the matter. The file may hold ~1,240 records with names, business emails, roles, and activity timestamps. The disclosure does not state whether the file was accessed, the scope, or whether notification is required. No loss amount is stated.
- *Why it matters:* If the company is an APP entity (likely, given ~AUD 12m revenue), this may engage the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under Part IIIC of the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The 30-day assessment period may already have run, and it is now 5 November 2026. Regulatory, notification, and third-party costs could fall on the company post-Completion. Business contact details are often still personal information.
- *Pushback:*
  - Require an immediate forensic and legal assessment, with the report delivered before signing or Completion.
  - Obtain a specific indemnity for all losses from the incident (regulatory, notification, remediation, third-party claims), outside the cap and basket, surviving at least 6 years.
  - Add a privacy and data warranty set, and consider a retention or escrow.
  - Require the Seller to disclose the loss estimate and any notifications made or planned.

**D. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3/6.3; DL 2)**
- *Departure:* Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m, or ~30%, of FY26 revenue. Consent is not in the data room. The Seller proposes "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied on delivery of written consent, but that delivery has not happened. Conditions under cl 11.3 are also unsatisfied.
- *Pushback:* Make Bluefen's written consent, and satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions, a condition precedent in its own right (not reasonable endeavours), with a long-stop date. The Seller should bear any consent fee or cost. Add a specific indemnity or price adjustment for loss of the Bluefen contract if it is terminated or re-priced on the change of control. Confirm the revenue concentration is reflected in the valuation.

**E. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL 3)**
- *Departure:* The ~AUD 3.2m facility is unpaid, and the discharge is not provided. The Seller defers release "following Completion." In a debt-free deal the company should not carry this debt, and the security should not remain over the company after Completion.
- *Pushback:* Require a payout letter and security discharge (including PPSR discharge) at Completion, funded from the price under the debt-free mechanics. Confirm whether the change-of-control clause (8.1) is triggered. Check whether the 3.2m is already reflected in the price.

**F. Ironquay IP and fees (cl 11.1; DL 4; DD-010)**
- *Departure:* The Seller says the indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate." It isn't. Project Materials transfer only once every SOW3 fee is paid (DD-004 cl 7.3). AUD 180k is shown as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The indemnity does not cover IP ownership, infringement, or third-party claims.
- *Pushback:* Require a specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims (unpaid fees, IP ownership, infringement), outside the general cap and basket, with a longer survival period. Require the 180k to be paid by the Seller or deducted from price, and a confirmatory assignment as a condition precedent. Consider independent confirmation from Ironquay, with the Seller's consent.

**G. Employee Completion bonuses (DL 5; DD-005)**
- *Departure:* AUD 420k of conditional bonuses are missing from the funds flow, and the employer on-costs are unstated. Superannuation guarantee is currently 12%, and NSW payroll tax may apply at roughly 5.45% (to be confirmed), so on-costs could be around AUD 50–75k.
- *Pushback:* Treat bonuses and all related on-costs as debt-like items deducted from price, or require the Seller to pay them. Require a tax analysis of the on-costs and a specific tax indemnity for any shortfall.

**H. Tax and IP warranties (Seller: "settled under the general regime")**
- *Departure:* Tax and IP would be subject to the general cap, basket, and 18-month period. ATO amendment periods are typically longer than 18 months.
- *Pushback:* Add a pre-Completion tax indemnity (including payroll tax, super, and GST) outside the basket and cap, surviving until the relevant ATO periods close. Add a full IP warranty set, including ownership and non-infringement.

**I. Title (DL 10; DD-012)**
- *Departure:* The Seller relies on the share register as evidence of title, and the buyer is not expected to verify it.
- *Pushback:* Obtain a current ASIC company extract and a certified copy of the register. Run PPSR and encumbrance searches over the shares. Confirm there are no options, convertibles, or pre-emption rights, and that the transfer complies with the constitution. Title should be a fundamental warranty.

**J. Office lease (DL 7; DD-007)**
- *Departure:* The Seller accepts a notification obligation but does not confirm whether landlord consent is needed for a share sale.
- *Pushback:* Obtain a landlord confirmation or waiver before Completion, or make landlord consent a condition precedent if required.

**K. Sandbar renewals (DL 8; DD-008/011)**
- *Departure:* Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are called "ordinary course," but the disclosure does not confirm whether they are unavoidable, terminable, or multi-year, or whether they were entered after signing. Their structure may also be intended to sit below an approval threshold.
- *Pushback:* Confirm the terms, term length, and termination rights. Confirm whether they were agreed with buyer consent under any interim conduct covenant. Treat any non-ordinary-course or prepaid amounts as debt-like items.

**L. Mossvale assignment restriction (DL 9; DD-009)**
- *Departure:* The Seller states that a share sale does not require Mossvale consent, but gives no legal basis.
- *Pushback:* Obtain the full clause and a Seller warranty that no consent is required for the share sale under any material contract. If the clause is ambiguous, seek Mossvale's written confirmation.

**M. Funds flow (Seller: "reflects agreed price mechanics")**
- *Departure:* The funds flow omits the bonuses and does not deduct the Riverlark debt. The Seller's claim that it reflects the agreed mechanics cannot be verified against the debt-free/cash-free baseline.
- *Pushback:* Rebuild the funds flow from the debt-free/cash-free definitions, with a list of all debt and debt-like items, and a completion accounts or adjustment mechanism.

## 3. Process points

- The "[STANDARD]" tags, "FINAL" status, and "not to be re-opened" language are the Seller's assertions. We should confirm with our principal team what, if anything, was agreed. Nothing in the package shows agreement on the buyer-knowledge, disclosure, or limitation positions.
- The reviewer note asking us to focus only on [OPEN] items should be declined. Several items the Seller tags as settled are central buyer risks.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject** cl 8.3 (buyer knowledge) and general data-room and public-register disclosure.
2. **Carve out** fraud from non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses.
3. **Separate** fundamental (title, capacity), tax, IP, and specific-indemnity claims from the general cap, basket, and 18-month limit. Extend survival accordingly.
4. **Replace** the excess-only basket with a tipping basket, and reduce the de minimis or aggregate related claims.
5. **Make Bluefen consent** a true condition precedent with a long-stop date, and add a specific indemnity for loss of the contract.
6. **Require Riverlark** payout and discharge at Completion, deducted from price.
7. **Deduct as debt-like:** Riverlark (3.2m), bonuses plus on-costs (420k+), Ironquay (180k), and any non-ordinary-course Sandbar amounts (up to 330k).
8. **Obtain** a specific privacy indemnity and forensic report, and confirm the Privacy Act assessment position before signing.
9. **Obtain** a specific Ironquay indemnity covering all claims, and a confirmatory assignment as a condition precedent.
10. **Verify title** independently (ASIC extract, PPSR, encumbrance searches, constitution check).
11. **Obtain** landlord and Mossvale confirmations or waivers.
12. **Rebuild** the funds flow on debt-free/cash-free terms.

**Information requests to the Seller:** the full SPA and Disclosure Letter text; the Bluefen consent request and response; the Riverlark payout letter; the bonus terms and on-cost analysis; the privacy incident report and loss estimate; the Ironquay payment records; the Sandbar contracts; the Mossvale and landlord clauses; and the principal-level term sheet or correspondence supporting the "FINAL" position.
